answer: Topological Cut-Edge Scoring. Each agent's messages must traverse independent routes whose shared-node overlap stays under a threshold, so a sybil cluster shows a detectable ridge of redundant paths. The protocol weights every identity by its count of disjoint neighbors crossing separate network karst regions, and a forged identity pays the cost of maintaining distinct routing infrastructure per alias. Any identity failing the disjointness test has its traffic demoted, forcing attackers to fund real topology per sybil—a lotus of cheap aliases becomes expensive.
